According to learned A.G.A. information of this bail application has been given to the victim on
17.3.2023, but no one has entered appearance.
2. Heard Shams Tabrez Ali, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Sunil Kumar Sriastava, learned A.G.A. and perused the record.

3. The applicant has approached this Court by way of filing the present Criminal Misc. Bail Application seeking enlargement on bail in Case Crime No.701 of 2022, under Sections 363, 366,
376 I.P.C. and Section 3/4 Protection of Children from Sexual Offence (POCSO) Act, 2012, Police Station-Kotwali Lalitpur, District-Lalitpur after rejection of his Bail Application vide order dated 19.12.2022 passed by Incharge Additional Sessions/Special Judge, (POCSO Act), Laitpur.

sentences.text: 5. Initially, F.I.R. was lodged on 17.10.2022 under Section 363 I.P.C. by the mother of victim that present applicant and co-accused namely Sonu have kidnapped her daughter from her lawful guardianship and she has not been traced.

6. Learned counsel for applicant submits that it appears that she was recovered on the same date and recorded under statements under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C.
7.

Learned counsel further submitted that under Section 161 Cr.P.C. she has stated that she left her house on her own will and met the present applicant and she agreed that she will marry her,
therefore, they entered into physical relationship.

8. Learned counsel further submitted that in the statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C.,
victim has stated that she knew applicant for last one year and she called the applicant and went along with him under the promise of marriage and applicant has committed wrong thing with her.
9. Learned counsel lastly referred medical examination of victim that it has not corroborated the allegations of physical relationship.
He further submitted that it was case of consensual relationship and applicant has not committed any crime.

Applicant is languishing in jail since 20.1.2023, there is no likelihood of early disposal of trial and the applicant undertakes that if enlarged on bail, he will never misuse his liberty and will co-operate in the trial.
10.Learned A.G.A. has opposed the bail application and submitted that age of the victim is 14 years and few months, therefore, consent, if any, is immaterial.
At this stage only on the basis of victim's medical examination, her statements recorded under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. may not be ignored.
11.LAW ON BAIL - A SUMMARY (A) The basic rule may perhaps be tersely put as bail, not jail.

(B) Power to grant bail under Section 439 Cr.P.C., is of wide amplitude but not an unfettered discretion, which calls for exercise in a judicious manner and not as a matter of course or in whimsical manner.

(C) While passing an order on an application for grant of bail, there is no need to record elaborate details to give an impression that the case is one that would result in a conviction or, by contrast, in an acquittal.

However, a Court cannot completely divorce its decision from material aspects of the case such as allegations made against accused; nature and gravity of accusation; having common object or intention; severity of punishment if allegations are proved beyond reasonable doubt and would result in a conviction; reasonable apprehension of witnesses being influenced by accused;
tampering of evidence; character, behaviour, means, position and standing of accused; likelihood of offence being repeated; the frivolity in the case of prosecution; criminal antecedents of accused and a prima facie satisfaction of Court in support of charge against accused.

The Court may also take note of participation or part of an unlawful assembly as well as that circumstantial evidence not being a ground to grant bail, if the evidence/ material collected establishes prima facie a complete chain of events.

sentences.text: In the present case, age of the victim is determined to be about 14 years and few months on the basis of her educational documents which cannot be doubted at this stage in the absence of any contrary material.

13. Statement of the victim recorded under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C, are consistent against the applicant that he has promised to marry her, therefore, they have entered into physical relationship.

However, considering the definition of 'Child' as defined under Section 2(d) of POCSO Act as well as contents of Section 375-Sixthly I.P.C., consent of a child i.e. a girl below 18 years, if any is immaterial.

14. At this stage, even considering the medical examination of victim which has prima-facie not supported the prosecution case, still this Court cannot ignore her statement recorded under Sections 161 Cr.P.C. and specifically under Section 164 Cr.P.C. which remained consistent against the applicant.

There is another factor which goes against the applicant that since the applicant is well acquainted with victim and till date, her statement has not been recorded during trial and that in case of bail, there would be reasonable apprehension that applicant may influence the victim,
therefore, while rejecting this bail application, Trial Court is directed to take all endeavour to record the statement of victim preferably within a period of three months from today, if there is no legal impediment.
